teaching.hint: What parts of a chosen subarray can lie between its first and last touched copies?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A range spanning copies consists of one suffix, some complete middle copies, and one prefix; only the sign of the complete-copy sum decides whether more middle copies help.
solution_outline.approach: For k=1, find the ordinary maximum subarray sum with zero allowed. For k>=2, find the maximum on two copies. Add (k-2) times the original total only when that total is positive. Apply the modulus after maximizing ordinary sums.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The two-copy optimum covers both single-copy ranges and suffix-plus-prefix ranges; the original total measures the gain of every additional whole middle copy.
solution_outline.correctness: Every range has the stated decomposition. Nonpositive middle copies can be removed without lowering its sum, so two copies suffice. If total T>0 and an internal optimum M has outside pieces A,B with A+B=T-M, the best suffix plus prefix is at least (M+A)+(M+B)=M+T>M. Thus the doubled optimum is boundary-crossing and can gain exactly (k-2)T by adding all middle copies. This attains the bound for every range shape.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space if two copies are scanned virtually. Sums before modulo may reach about 10^14.
solution_outline.pitfall: Reducing sums modulo the modulus before comparing maxima changes their order and invalidates the optimization.

common_wrong_turns: Reducing sums modulo the modulus before comparing maxima changes their order and invalidates the optimization.
source_fidelity_notes: Preserved conceptual repetition, k=1, empty ranges, negatives, and final modulo; distinguished separate copies from circular-buffer reuse restrictions.
